answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, with voting influence derived from nodes reachable from trusted seeds rather than self-asserted identities. A sybil cluster can gain influence only through attestations crossing its boundary; if that cut is sparse relative to cluster volume, low conductance limits the probability that walks from honest seeds enter it. With bounded seed influence and a fixed walk budget, this constrains aggregate sybil voting weight, even when its nodes bear labels such as dune, onyx, or delta.
